items.label: Industry: AI GPU Cloud Infrastructure ("Neoclouds")
items.detail: Selected via account-grounded holdings: the IBKR connector was authenticated this session, and the account directly holds CRWV (CoreWeave, 150 sh, $13,117 market value, Trading Sleeve) plus adjacent power-buildout exposure via GEV (GE Vernova, 20 sh, $19,134). Neoclouds -- GPU-specialized cloud providers such as CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Nscale, and IREN -- are one of the most consistently cited fast-moving AI-infrastructure themes in September 2026: category size estimates range from $20-42B in 2026 to $180-254B by 2030-2031 across sources (46-56% CAGR), and this month's earnings commentary shows the competitive frontier shifting from GPU procurement to power/energy access ("power wars"). Not covered by any prior scout cycle (critical minerals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13, nuclear/SMR 2026-09-20).

items.label: GEV
items.detail: GE Vernova -- held, 20 sh, $19,134.40 market value (+$410.80 unrealized, Trading Sleeve). This run's neocloud research reinforces GEV's power-equipment thesis with concrete new demand evidence: CoreWeave is targeting 1.7 GW of active power by year-end 2026, Nebius is targeting up to 1 GW of connected capacity against 4+ GW of contracted power, and September 2026 sector earnings commentary explicitly frames competition as having shifted "from the GPU race to power wars" -- meaning gas turbines, grid interconnects, and on-site generation (GE Vernova's core product lines) are now the binding constraint on AI-cloud capacity growth, not chip supply. Real risk: GEV's backlog is not neocloud-specific, so a broader AI-capex slowdown (see the compute-oversupply watch item below) or a shift toward on-site solar/battery instead of gas turbines would hit its growth rate, and the stock already trades at a premium multiple pricing in continued acceleration.

items.label: NBIS
items.detail: Nebius Group -- not held. The clearest large-scale neocloud alternative to CoreWeave with a more diversified customer book: a roughly $40B contracted backlog anchored by a $27B five-year Meta deal and a $17.4B Microsoft deal, 2026 guidance of $3.0-3.4B revenue and $7-9B exit ARR, and Q2 2026 revenue up 454% YoY to $582.3M. Stock last $238.38 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-09-27), down roughly 22% over the trailing month on balance-sheet stress and equity-dilution fears even as the underlying contract book has grown -- a genuine disconnect between operating momentum and share price worth evaluating now rather than chasing a re-rate. Real risk: like CoreWeave, Nebius is funding gigawatt-scale buildouts against contracts that assume sustained hyperscaler demand; a Meta or Microsoft capacity pullback would hit concentrated revenue hard, and near-term execution hinges on November 2026 Q3 results confirming contracted power capacity is tracking toward 5 GW by year-end.
items.suggested_size: Starter position, sized against existing CRWV exposure to avoid doubling neocloud-specific execution risk within the Trading Sleeve.

items.label: IREN
items.detail: IREN Ltd -- not held. A former Bitcoin miner's AI-cloud pivot offering exposure to the same GPU-leasing economics as CoreWeave/Nebius through an operator with an unusually fast contract ramp: a $9.7B five-year Microsoft AI cloud deal (~$1.9B ARR at 85% EBITDA margins), a $3.4B five-year NVIDIA managed-GPU-cloud contract, and a raised year-end-2026 AI Cloud ARR target above $4B (up from $3.7B), with the GPU fleet scaling from 23,000 to 140,000 units. Stock last $44.12 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-09-27), still roughly 40% off its 52-week high despite a 17-20% single-day rally on the July 2026 Microsoft contract news -- volatility reflecting genuine disagreement over whether a crypto-miner-turned-neocloud can execute at this pace. Real risk: the heaviest debt/capex load of this cycle's group relative to its balance-sheet history (the $1.6B Dell/Blackwell GPU purchase alone), and far less operating history as a cloud/data-center business than any peer here.
items.suggested_size: Small speculative starter given execution/debt-load risk; size meaningfully smaller than NBIS or a CRWV add.

items.label: VRT
items.detail: Vertiv Holdings -- not held. A picks-and-shovels play one layer removed from any single neocloud's customer-concentration or debt risk: Vertiv supplies power and thermal-management equipment (liquid cooling, UPS, switchgear) to CoreWeave, Nebius, hyperscalers, and traditional enterprise data centers alike, so it benefits from the sector-wide "power wars" shift surfaced in this cycle's research regardless of which individual neocloud wins or loses share. Stock last $253.30 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-09-27). Real risk: Vertiv's order book is itself a leading indicator of AI-capex sentiment -- if the compute-oversupply case below plays out and hyperscalers/neoclouds slow build-outs, Vertiv's backlog decelerates in lockstep, and it already trades at a full multiple pricing in continued AI-infrastructure capex growth.
items.suggested_size: Diversification-oriented satellite position -- lower correlation to CRWV-specific balance-sheet risk than adding to a direct neocloud name.
items.diversification_note: Reduces reliance on any single neocloud's execution/debt risk while keeping exposure to the same AI-infrastructure capex cycle already represented by CRWV and GEV.

items.label: CRWV
items.detail: CoreWeave -- held, 150 sh, $13,117.50 market value (+$315.50 unrealized, Trading Sleeve). This run's research surfaces a real, current risk rather than cleanly reinforcing the thesis: total debt (ex-leases) is roughly $24.9B, with about $7.5B secured directly against GPU collateral subject to accelerating depreciation, and analysts flag loan covenants that could trip as early as 2027 if chip valuations fall faster than assumed -- a live concern given GPU rental rates have already dropped 50-70% from peak. Against that, the backlog is real and diversifying: Microsoft's share of revenue has fallen from roughly 67% as OpenAI (~$22.4B), Meta (~$35.2B implied), Anthropic, and Jane Street add capacity commitments, and 2026 guidance calls for $31-35B of capex against ~$6.2B trailing-12-month revenue -- an aggressive but demand-backed build-out, not an empty one. Net: track Q4 2026/Q1 2027 results for the first real test of whether the GPU-collateral depreciation assumptions hold before treating this as either a reinforced thesis or a red flag.

items.label: GPU depreciation & debt-collateral risk (sector-wide)
items.detail: No specific new ticker -- a theme-level accounting/financing risk sitting underneath every debt-funded neocloud in this cycle's set (CRWV most acutely, but also IREN's Dell/Blackwell-funded buildout and Nebius's capex-heavy backlog): GPU rental/spot rates have fallen 50-70% from peak, shrinking the collateral value backing billions in debt secured against depreciating chips just as covenant tests and repayment schedules begin referencing that lower valuation. This is a live, dated risk (analysts flag 2027 as the earliest covenant-trip window for CoreWeave specifically), not a hypothetical -- worth tracking earnings commentary from all three neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS, IREN) each quarter rather than pricing in as a blanket discount to any one name.

items.label: AI compute oversupply / bubble debate
items.detail: No specific ticker -- a genuine, unresolved debate directly relevant to every name in this cycle's set: Omdia data shows token demand jumping from roughly 6M tokens/minute (Oct 2025) to roughly 15B (March 2026), supporting a shortage narrative, while Goldman Sachs' Delta One desk and a Trump science-and-technology adviser have both separately warned of a 2028-2029 compute-glut risk window if output costs fall faster than consumption grows -- and Meta became the first hyperscaler to publicly admit 'excess compute capacity' in July 2026. This cuts directly against the capex-growth assumption embedded in CRWV, NBIS, IREN, GEV, and VRT valuations alike; worth tracking hyperscaler capex-guidance language each quarter for the first signs of a demand-side slowdown rather than assuming the current buildout pace is a permanent baseline.

items.label: Nvidia chip export-control & tariff regime (China)
items.detail: No specific ticker -- a regulatory swing factor for the whole GPU supply chain that indirectly affects every name here: as of January 2026, BIS shifted H200/MI325X export-license review for China from presumption-of-denial to case-by-case, subject to a 25% tariff, a 50%-of-US-volume cap, and revenue-sharing with the US government (extending an August 2025 15% arrangement) -- easing some chip-supply tightness globally versus 2025's outright restrictions, but leaving allocation politically contingent and reversible. Further loosening would ease the GPU-scarcity dynamic that has underpinned neocloud pricing power; a tightening or Chinese retaliation would cut the other way. Track BIS rule changes each quarter alongside Nvidia's own allocation commentary.
